title: Review of Criteria for Lease Buyback Scheme
what_it_is: Review of Criteria for Lease Buyback Scheme

sections.label: Lease Buyback Scheme exceptions
sections.summary: HDB has exercised flexibility for about 50 households since April 2015, with the main rejection reason being failure to meet the age requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) since 2009, whether exceptions to the rules for the Lease Buyback scheme have been exercised by HDB for applicants with unique circumstances; (b) if so, how many have been approved; (c) what have been the main reasons for rejection since the scheme's extension to 4-room flats since April 2015; and (d) whether HDB will exercise flexibility when only one of the spouse qualifies under the age criterion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This comprises 830 households in 4-room flats, 2,030 households in 3-room flats, and the remaining 240 households in smaller flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Among those who asked for exceptions to the LBS criteria, the main reason for rejection is that they do not meet the age requirement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The qualifying age for LBS is set at the Central Provident Fund (CPF) Payout Eligibility Age of 65 to allow seniors to immediately receive their monthly CPF payouts when they take up the LBS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That said, the Housing and Development Board (HDB) has exercised flexibility for applicants based on their individual circumstances, such as ill health or financial difficulty, and has done so for about 50 households since April 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This includes households who did not meet the age requirement.

sections.label: Resident's Lease Buyback rejection
sections.summary: A Member cites a resident aged 65 and going blind who received a third rejection because HDB said she is 62.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The reason I ask is because there was an answer in the Forum Page in The Straits Times that HDB will consider some flexibility.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: But then, last week, I received a third rejection for my resident who is aged 65 and going blind.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: HDB just said that because she is 62, they cannot do the Lease Buyback Scheme.

sections.label: Case can be raised separately
sections.summary: The Minister says the specific case can be looked at if the Member raises it separately.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, I just want to know how it is considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We can look at the case in specific if the Member would raise it to me separately.
